meta.coverage: Dallas–Fort Worth: in-city Dallas and Fort Worth neighborhoods, North Dallas, Collin County, the East lakes and the West Mid-Cities
meta.method: Editorial profiles written from local knowledge and public sources. Scores are 0–5 relative comparisons inside this coverage area, not ratings. Price tiers are relative. Home values come from public Zillow data on the Market page; NTREIS/MLS data is not used.

score_keys.new_construction: Share of newer (2010+) and new-build homes
score_keys.lot_size: Typical lot size; higher means larger lots and acreage
score_keys.amenities: Density of dining, retail and entertainment nearby
score_keys.commute_north: Ease of reaching the Legacy/Plano/Frisco job corridors
score_keys.value: More home for the money; higher means lower relative price

meta.commute_source: Off-peak drive estimates from OpenStreetMap routing (OSRM), measured from each area's center on 2026-10-21. Rush hour is often much longer.
meta.tax_source: 2025 tax rates per $100 of value, from Republic Title's 2025 DFW Area Tax Rates (compiled from county appraisal districts). County column includes county, community college and hospital districts where they apply. Excludes MUD/PID and special districts, and is before homestead exemptions.

neighborhoods.name: Frisco
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1995–present; active new construction on the north side
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots in master-planned communities; larger lots in select enclaves
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs are the norm, often with amenity centers and pools
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Some newer communities sit in MUD or PID districts that add to the tax rate. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Strong for Legacy/Plano and Frisco job centers. Downtown Dallas is a Tollway drive that is longer at peak hours.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing mixed-use growth along the Tollway and SH 121, including the PGA of America headquarters at Fields and Universal's family theme park project. Verify current timelines.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Frisco is the default answer for many relocating buyers: newer homes, big-league sports and entertainment, and a deep bench of master-planned communities with amenity centers.
pros: Entertainment and dining density for a suburb
Close to the Legacy and SH 121 job corridors
cons: Tollway traffic and toll costs to Dallas
MUD/PID districts can raise carrying costs
Pricing is competitive for move-up buyers

neighborhoods.name: West Plano
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1980s–2000s; urban product at Legacy West and Legacy Town Center
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Established suburban lots with mature trees
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix of mandatory and voluntary HOAs; many older sections have light or no HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city with no MUD/PID districts in most resale areas. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Next to major corporate campuses at Legacy. The Tollway gives a direct line to Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Continued corporate and mixed-use activity around Legacy. Verify specific projects before quoting.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Established, centrally located and close to big employers. You get mature neighborhoods without a far-north commute.
pros: Central to North Dallas job centers

neighborhoods.name: Downtown & East Plano
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1960s–1980s single-family; newer infill near downtown
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Modest suburban lots; some larger older lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city tax structure. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 and DART rail from Downtown Plano station give a car-optional path to Richardson and Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented infill around Downtown Plano station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: One of the few places in Collin County with a walkable historic downtown and light rail, at a lower entry price than West Plano.
pros: Lower entry price than West Plano

neighborhoods.name: McKinney
neighborhoods.home_age: Historic core (early 1900s) through active new construction to the north and west
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Varied: historic lots downtown, master-planned lots, acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities; historic district has preservation rules instead
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Several newer communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Craig Ranch and the SH 121 side reach Legacy and Frisco easily. The north and east sides mean longer drives to Dallas.
neighborhoods.development: Steady growth along SH 121 and US 380. Watch planned roadway projects on US 380 for commute impact.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: McKinney has a real historic downtown, plus everything from 1900s homes to brand-new master plans. It often gets you more house than Frisco or Allen.
pros: Wide range of price points and home ages
Often more space per dollar than Frisco
cons: Longer commute to Dallas from the north side
MUD/PID taxes in some new communities

neighborhoods.name: Allen
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1990s–2010s
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common, typically moderate dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Mostly established resale areas. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 runs straight to Richardson and Dallas. SH 121 reaches Frisco and Legacy.
neighborhoods.development: Mixed-use along US 75 and SH 121.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Allen is a polished, mid-sized suburb with 1990s–2000s homes, strong retail and a central position on US 75.
best_for: Buyers who want newer suburban homes

neighborhoods.name: Prosper
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2005–present, with heavy new construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Larger-than-typical suburban lots; estate lots common
neighborhoods.hoa: Master-planned HOAs with large amenity packages are common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Many communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Get the full combined rate before you compare.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Tollway extension access. Frisco is close. Dallas is a long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Major retail and residential build-out along US 380 and the Tollway extension.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Prosper is newer, roomier and more upscale, with big master-planned amenities and a small-town center that is growing fast.
pros: Close to Frisco without its density
cons: Retail still catching up in places

neighborhoods.name: Celina
neighborhoods.home_age: Overwhelmingly new construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Master-planned lots plus rural acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: Master-planned HOAs (e.g., Light Farms, Mustang Lakes) with large amenity packages
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are very common. Compare the total rate, not the base city rate.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Dallas North Tollway extensions are bringing it closer. Today it is a long drive to Dallas and a moderate one to Frisco.
neighborhoods.development: One of the region's fastest-growing cities. Roads, retail and schools are all being built out.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Celina is the far-north frontier: brand-new homes and big amenity communities, for buyers who accept today's drive.
cons: Longest commute to Dallas in this set

neighborhoods.name: Richardson
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1950s–1980s, with newer infill and urban product at CityLine
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Generous mid-century lots with mature trees
neighborhoods.hoa: Many neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Established city tax structure. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: One of the best-connected suburbs. US 75, the Bush Turnpike and several DART stations reach Dallas and Plano.
neighborhoods.development: Corporate campuses at CityLine and transit-oriented development around rail stations. The DART Silver Line adds east-west rail; confirm current service.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Richardson offers mid-century homes on big leafy lots, great transit and quick access to Dallas, at prices below the Collin County new-build belt.
cons: Mixed ISD boundaries; verify by address

neighborhoods.name: Far North Dallas
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–1990s
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots; many townhome and condo communities
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies widely; condos and townhomes carry HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas and Dallas County rates. Collin County portions differ, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Tollway gives a straight shot to Uptown and to Legacy, so it is central for two-job households.
neighborhoods.development: Redevelopment and refreshes around older retail centers.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Far North Dallas is one of the most central addresses for split commutes, with City of Dallas services and a wide mix of housing types.
cons: ISD and county boundaries vary block to block

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

tax.note: Parts of Far North Dallas are in Plano ISD or Richardson ISD, which changes the school portion.

neighborhoods.name: Preston Hollow
neighborhoods.home_age: Mid-century originals alongside extensive new luxury construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Large lots, including some of Dallas's biggest in-city estates
neighborhoods.hoa: Mostly no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas / Dallas County. Taxes scale with high values.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Minutes to Uptown, Downtown and Love Field. One of the shortest luxury commutes in the region.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing teardown/rebuild of luxury homes and redevelopment around Preston Center.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Preston Hollow means estate lots, luxury new builds and a short drive to everything in central Dallas.
pros: Very short commute to the urban core
cons: Teardown economics drive much of the market

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Addison
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1980s–2000s, with newer townhome infill
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Small lots; townhome and urban formats dominate
neighborhoods.hoa: Most townhomes and condos carry HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Addison has a notably low city rate. Total tax still depends on ISD and county.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Tollway access, and the DART Silver Line connects east-west. Confirm current service status.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented development planned around the Addison Silver Line station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A small town with a big restaurant scene. Lock-and-leave townhomes and condos sit minutes from the Tollway.

neighborhoods.name: Carrollton
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–1990s; newer infill near Downtown Carrollton
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many older neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Spans three counties, so rates vary by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Multiple highways plus the DART Green Line, with Silver Line connections at Downtown Carrollton.
neighborhoods.development: Transit-oriented development at Downtown Carrollton station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Practical, well-connected and less expensive than the Collin County new-build belt, with a rail-served downtown square.
cons: Three counties mean varied tax rates

neighborhoods.name: The Colony
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–1990s, with newer pockets
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; lakefront and lake-adjacent options
neighborhoods.hoa: Many older areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Denton County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: SH 121 reaches Frisco, Plano and the Legacy corridor quickly. Dallas is a longer drive.
neighborhoods.development: Grandscape's entertainment and retail district continues to expand.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lake access and Grandscape's entertainment at prices below neighboring Frisco.

neighborhoods.name: Little Elm
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2000s–present
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots; lake-adjacent options
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Some newer communities sit in MUD/PID districts. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Frisco is close. Dallas is a long drive. FM 423 and US 380 get congested.
neighborhoods.development: Lakefront district growth and new subdivisions.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Newer homes near the lake with a beach-town feel and a lower entry price than Frisco next door.

rows.label: Little Elm (Denton County, Little Elm ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Wylie
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2000s–present; historic downtown core
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots, with larger lots toward Lake Lavon
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address; some newer areas carry special districts.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: SH 78 and the Bush Turnpike lead to Garland, Richardson and Dallas. The north-corridor job centers are a longer drive.
neighborhoods.development: Steady residential growth on the east side of Collin County.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Small-town feel and newer homes near Lake Lavon at moderate prices.
cons: Far from the Legacy/Frisco job corridors

neighborhoods.name: Murphy
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2000s
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to larger suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Bush Turnpike is close for Richardson and Plano. Legacy is a moderate drive.
neighborhoods.development: Mostly built out; limited new subdivisions.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A small, mostly residential suburb of 2000s homes with an east-Plano address feel.
cons: Mixed ISD boundaries; verify by address
best_for: Buyers who want a mostly residential area

neighborhoods.name: Lucas & Fairview
neighborhoods.home_age: 1990s–present custom homes
neighborhoods.lot_profile: One acre and up is common in Lucas; Fairview mixes acreage with town-center living
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies; many acreage properties have light or no HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Check by address; some properties may carry agricultural valuations. Verify before purchase.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 is close for Allen and Plano. Dallas is a moderate-to-long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Limited, low-density growth by design.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Room to breathe: acreage, custom homes and quiet country roads, still close to Allen and Plano.

neighborhoods.name: Anna & Melissa
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2010s–present new construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots; acreage at the edges
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in new communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are common in new communities. Compare total rates.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 75 south to McKinney, Allen and Plano. Dallas is a long drive.
neighborhoods.development: Rapid builder activity and new retail along US 75.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The most accessible entry point to new-construction Collin County living, with builder incentives often in play.
pros: Lowest entry price in this set

neighborhoods.name: Princeton
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 2015–present new construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard master-planned lots
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in new communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: MUD/PID districts are common. Compare total rates.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: US 380 west to McKinney and US 75. Dallas is a long drive, and US 380 congestion is the main tradeoff.
neighborhoods.development: Very rapid residential growth. Watch planned US 380 improvements.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: New homes at entry prices on the east side of Collin County, for buyers who prioritize space and price over commute.

neighborhoods.name: Rockwall
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1990s–present, with active new construction
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to large lots; lakefront and lake-view options
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common in newer communities
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Rockwall County rates. Some newer areas carry special districts, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: I-30 runs west across Lake Ray Hubbard into Dallas. Peak-hour bridge traffic is the main tradeoff.
neighborhoods.development: Steady residential and retail growth along I-30 and SH 205.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lakeside living east of Dallas, with The Harbor's waterfront dining and a small-town square.
cons: I-30 bridge traffic at peak hours
Far from the north job corridors

neighborhoods.name: Rowlett
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1980s–2000s, with newer pockets
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; many lake-adjacent streets
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix; many older areas have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas/Rockwall county rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: The Bush Turnpike and I-30 reach Dallas and Richardson. The DART Blue Line ends at Downtown Rowlett.
neighborhoods.development: Sapphire Bay, a planned lakefront resort district, has housing built but its resort pieces remain unbuilt. The city issued a notice of default to the developer in January 2026.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lake-adjacent homes at moderate prices, with a rail line into Dallas.

neighborhoods.name: Garland
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1950s–1990s, with newer infill
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Many neighborhoods have no mandatory HOA
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas County rates. Garland Power & Light is a city-owned utility, so most residents don't shop for electricity providers.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Several freeways plus DART Blue Line stations reach Dallas and Richardson.
neighborhoods.development: Downtown Garland redevelopment around the square and rail station.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: One of the most affordable places close to Dallas, with rail access and a revitalized downtown.
pros: Lower entry prices close to Dallas
cons: Big city with very different neighborhoods

neighborhoods.name: Grapevine
neighborhoods.home_age: Historic core plus 1980s–2000s neighborhoods
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard lots; larger lots near the lake
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies; historic areas have preservation rules
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Mostly Tarrant County. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Next to DFW Airport. SH 114 and SH 121 reach Dallas, Las Colinas and Fort Worth. TEXRail runs from Grapevine Main to Fort Worth, and the DART Silver Line serves the airport area.
neighborhoods.development: Ongoing Main Street and lake-area investment; the city brands itself the Christmas Capital of Texas.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A historic Main Street with wineries and festivals, right next to DFW Airport.

neighborhoods.name: Flower Mound
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1990s–2010s
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Larger lots and preserved open space
neighborhoods.hoa: HOAs common
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Denton County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Close to DFW Airport and the SH 121 corridor. Dallas is a moderate drive.
neighborhoods.development: Low-density growth guided by the town's master plan.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Spacious and green, with larger lots and quick airport access.

neighborhoods.name: Las Colinas
neighborhoods.home_age: 1970s master plan to present, with lots of newer urban product
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Small to standard lots; many condo and townhome options
neighborhoods.hoa: Most condos and townhomes have HOA dues
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Dallas County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Central to DFW Airport, Dallas and the corporate offices in the Urban Center. DART's Orange Line serves Las Colinas.
neighborhoods.development: Continued office, hotel and residential growth in the Urban Center.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A master-planned business district with canals, lakes and lock-and-leave living between Dallas and the airport.
pros: Central between Dallas and the airport

neighborhoods.name: Arlington
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1970s–2000s, with newer areas to the south
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard suburban lots
neighborhoods.hoa: Mix of HOA and non-HOA neighborhoods
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Tarrant County rates. Check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Between Dallas and Fort Worth. Arlington uses on-demand rideshare transit (Via) instead of fixed bus routes.
neighborhoods.development: Continued growth around the Entertainment District.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Home of the Cowboys and Rangers: the entertainment capital of the metroplex, centrally placed between Dallas and Fort Worth.

neighborhoods.name: Fort Worth
neighborhoods.home_age: Everything from 1900s historic districts to brand-new suburbs
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Varies widely by neighborhood
neighborhoods.hoa: Varies widely
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Tarrant County rates. Some newer areas carry special districts, so check by address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Its own job center, with a downtown, medical district and industry. Dallas is a 45-minute-plus drive, so most residents work in Fort Worth.
neighborhoods.development: Large growth across the city, including Panther Island along the Trinity River and new master-planned suburbs.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: A big city with a Western heart: museums, the Stockyards, a lively downtown and neighborhoods at every price point.
cons: New suburbs can be far out

rows.label: City of Fort Worth (Tarrant County, Fort Worth ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Uptown & Victory Park
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1990s to present, with new towers still delivering and a few older homes in the State Thomas area.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Very small or no private lots; most homes are condos or townhomes on tight urban sites.
neighborhoods.hoa: Condo and townhome HOAs are nearly universal, and high-rise dues often cover concierge, amenities and building reserves.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. Properties inside the Uptown PID pay an added PID assessment. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown Dallas is minutes away by car, the free M-Line streetcar or DART. The Tollway leads north toward Legacy and Frisco, which is a longer drive at peak hours.
amenities: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
neighborhoods.development: Goldman Sachs is building an 800,000-square-foot Victory Park campus with a 1.5-acre park, expected to finish in 2028. Verify current timelines.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Uptown is Dallas's densest walkable district, with condo towers, restaurant-lined McKinney Avenue and the Katy Trail. Victory Park adds the arena, the Perot Museum and newer high-rises on the downtown edge.
cons: Event and weekend traffic and parking

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Oak Cliff & Bishop Arts
neighborhoods.home_age: Wide range: early 1900s homes in the historic districts, mid-century ranches, and newer infill near Bishop Arts.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Mix of standard city lots and larger hillside lots in areas like Kessler Park, with some tree-heavy, sloped sites.
neighborhoods.hoa: Most single-family streets have no mandatory HOA; city historic and conservation districts (such as Winnetka Heights) add exterior design rules.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. Historic-district homes may qualify for city preservation incentives. Check the exact address.
routes: Dallas Streetcar (Bishop Arts to Union Station)
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown is a short drive across the Trinity via I-35E or the Houston Street viaduct, and the Dallas Streetcar links Bishop Arts to Union Station. North job centers mean crossing downtown.
neighborhoods.development: Halperin Park, a deck park over I-35E next to the Dallas Zoo, opened its first phase in May 2026, with a second phase planned. Infill housing continues around Bishop Arts.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Oak Cliff was a separate town until Dallas annexed it in 1903 and keeps its own feel, with historic districts, hills and parks. Bishop Arts is its walkable core of independent shops, restaurants and galleries.
cons: Busy streets and parking around Bishop Arts
Housing stock varies block to block
best_for: Buyers seeking value near the core

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: East Dallas & Lakewood/White Rock
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1910s to 1950s in Lakewood and Old East Dallas, with ranch-era homes near the lake and scattered newer rebuilds.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to large city lots with mature trees; some larger lots near White Rock Lake and the Lakewood Country Club area.
neighborhoods.hoa: Most single-family streets have no mandatory HOA; city conservation and historic districts (including Swiss Avenue) set exterior rules in parts of the area.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. Check whether a home sits in a historic or conservation district, which can affect remodel plans.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown is about a 10-15 minute drive via Gaston, Swiss or I-30, and DART Blue Line stations sit on the west and north sides. Reaching Plano and Frisco means US 75 traffic.
neighborhoods.development: Mostly infill, including townhome projects along Gaston Avenue and teardown-rebuilds on older lots. Verify current projects.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: East Dallas wraps around White Rock Lake, with tree-lined streets of Craftsman, Tudor and Spanish-style homes in Lakewood and grand houses on Swiss Avenue. The lake's trail loop and the Arboretum are the big draws.
cons: Prices are high for lot and home age
best_for: Buyers wanting yard space near the core

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Lower Greenville & M Streets
neighborhoods.home_age: The M Streets (Greenland Hills) were mostly built in the 1920s and 1930s; newer mid-rise apartments line Greenville Avenue.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Narrow, standard city lots with alleys and mature trees; little room for large yards.
neighborhoods.hoa: No mandatory HOA on most streets; the M Streets conservation district sets rules for exterior changes and new builds.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. Conservation-district rules can affect rebuild and addition plans. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown and Uptown are a short drive down US 75 or Ross Avenue, and Mockingbird Station is close by for DART. US 75 is the route north to Richardson and Plano.
neighborhoods.development: Mid-rise apartment infill continues near Greenville Avenue, such as RangeWater's 236-unit project at 5714 Richmond Ave. Verify current projects.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lower Greenville is a long-running entertainment strip, anchored by the 1946 Granada Theater. Next to it, the M Streets are known for blocks of 1920s-30s Tudor cottages.
pros: Walk to restaurants and live music
cons: Weekend noise and parking near Greenville Ave

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Deep Ellum & Downtown Dallas
neighborhoods.home_age: Historic early-1900s commercial buildings converted to lofts, plus residential towers and apartments from the 2000s to present.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: No private lots to speak of; homes are condos and lofts in urban buildings.
neighborhoods.hoa: Condo HOAs are standard, and dues vary widely by building age and amenities.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. Downtown sits in the Downtown Dallas Improvement District and Deep Ellum has its own PID, both adding assessments. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: This is the regional hub: all DART light-rail lines meet downtown, and Deep Ellum has its own Green Line station. North job centers are reachable by US 75 or DART, with peak traffic.
neighborhoods.development: The $3.7 billion Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center rebuild broke ground in 2024, with construction expected through 2028. TxDOT's plan to lower I-345 into a trench could reshape the Downtown-Deep Ellum edge. Verify current timelines.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Downtown offers high-rise and loft living around parks, the Arts District and the rail hub. Deep Ellum, just east, is a historic warehouse district known for live music, murals and barbecue.
pros: Best rail access in the region
Range of loft and condo price points

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Lake Highlands
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1950s to 1970s ranch-style homes, with remodels and some newer builds.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Generous suburban-style lots by Dallas standards, many with mature trees and alleys.
neighborhoods.hoa: Most single-family areas have no mandatory HOA; voluntary neighborhood associations are common, and condos and townhomes carry HOA dues.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes; most of the area is in Richardson ISD. The Lake Highlands PID along the Skillman corridor assesses commercial and condo property.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: DART Blue Line stations (White Rock, Lake Highlands, LBJ/Skillman) run to Downtown, and LBJ and US 75 connect to Richardson and Plano job centers.
neighborhoods.development: In September 2026 the Dallas City Council approved TIF support for a small retail and office redevelopment at Walnut Hill Lane and Audelia Road. Verify current projects.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Lake Highlands is a postwar neighborhood of ranch homes on tree-lined streets, just north and east of White Rock Lake. It sits within Dallas city limits but is served mostly by Richardson ISD.
pros: Close to White Rock Lake trails
cons: Mix of school districts by address

rows.label: City of Dallas with Richardson ISD (Dallas County)

tax.note: Lake Highlands is in the City of Dallas but mostly served by Richardson ISD; the combined rate is the sum of the city, ISD and county rates shown.

neighborhoods.name: Knox-Henderson & Oak Lawn
neighborhoods.home_age: Mix of 1920s-50s homes and duplexes, 1960s-80s condos, and many townhomes and towers from the 2000s to present.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Small urban lots; most new construction is townhomes or multifamily replacing older homes.
neighborhoods.hoa: Condos and newer townhome rows usually have HOAs; older single-family streets typically do not.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. The Knox Street PID adds an assessment inside its boundary, and Oak Lawn is governed by its own special-purpose zoning district. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown and Uptown are a few minutes away by car, Katy Trail or DART. The Tollway and US 75 run north to Plano and Frisco, with peak congestion.
neighborhoods.development: The Knox, a roughly 1-million-square-foot project next to the Katy Trail, includes a 27-story apartment tower, a 140-room hotel with condos and an office building. The hotel and office are set for late 2026.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Knox-Henderson pairs a shopping and dining strip with the Katy Trail on either side of US 75. Oak Lawn, to the west, is a dense, central mix of condos, townhomes and the Cedar Springs dining corridor.
cons: Construction and traffic on Knox and Henderson

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Highland Park & University Park
neighborhoods.home_age: Original homes date from the 1910s-1940s, but many lots have been rebuilt with newer luxury homes.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to large lots, with bigger estate lots along Turtle Creek and in parts of Highland Park.
neighborhoods.hoa: No HOAs on most streets; each town has its own building and zoning rules, which are strict on new construction.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: Separate towns inside Dallas: the Town of Highland Park or City of University Park, plus Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College, with Highland Park ISD. A small part of Highland Park is in Dallas ISD. Check the exact address.
isd: Dallas ISD (small part of Highland Park)
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown and Uptown are a short drive down the Tollway or US 75, with DART at Mockingbird and Lovers Lane stations nearby. Legacy and Frisco are a Tollway drive north.
neighborhoods.development: SMU opened the $100 million Garry Weber End Zone Complex at Ford Stadium in 2024, and The Knox project on the Highland Park edge is set for late 2026.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The Park Cities are two separate towns surrounded by Dallas, with tree-lined streets, Turtle Creek parks and SMU. Highland Park Village, a 1931 Spanish-style center, is a National Historic Landmark.
pros: Own town services and school district
best_for: Buyers building new on an established lot

neighborhoods.name: Design District & Medical District / Love Field
neighborhoods.home_age: Design District housing is mostly 2010s to present; neighborhoods near Love Field are largely 1930s to 1960s single-family homes.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Urban infill sites in the Design District; standard city lots in the residential pockets near Love Field.
neighborhoods.hoa: Condos and townhomes carry HOAs; older single-family areas near Love Field generally do not.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Dallas, Dallas County, Parkland Hospital District and Dallas College levy property taxes alongside the ISD. The Oak Lawn-Hi Line PID covers part of the Design District area. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown is minutes away on I-35E or DART Green/Orange, which also serve the Medical District and Love Field. North job centers are reached via the Tollway or I-35E.
neighborhoods.development: Children's Health and UT Southwestern broke ground in 2024 on a $5 billion pediatric campus at Harry Hines and Mockingbird. Love Field expects to start a terminal and concourse expansion in 2027, and Hi Line Square is planned in the Design District. Verify current timelines.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The Design District grew from warehouses into showrooms, galleries, restaurants and apartments along the Trinity levee. Beyond it, the Southwestern Medical District and Love Field form a major job and travel hub.
pros: Close to Downtown and the hospitals
cons: Airport and freeway noise in places
Mostly rental and condo housing in the core
Limited grocery and daily retail in pockets

rows.label: City of Dallas (Dallas County, Dallas ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Near Southside & Magnolia
neighborhoods.home_age: Late-1800s to 1920s homes in Fairmount, plus apartment and townhome infill from the 2010s to present.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard older city lots with alleys; infill sites are small and dense.
neighborhoods.hoa: Most single-family homes have no HOA; the Fairmount historic district sets exterior design rules.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Tarrant County Hospital District (JPS), Tarrant County College and Tarrant Regional Water District levy property taxes alongside Fort Worth ISD. Fairmount homes may qualify for city historic-preservation incentives. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown Fort Worth is just north, and T&P Station (TRE and TEXRail) is nearby. Dallas is a 45-minute-plus drive or a TRE ride; Legacy and Frisco are far.
neighborhoods.development: Trinity Metro plans to extend TEXRail 2.1 miles from T&P Station to a Medical District station, with groundbreaking targeted for late 2026 and opening around 2029. UT Southwestern broke ground on a cancer center in the Near Southside in 2025.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The Near Southside mixes Fort Worth's hospital district with Magnolia Avenue's restaurants and bars. Fairmount, one of the Southwest's largest historic districts, holds most of the older homes.
pros: Close to Downtown and the hospitals

rows.label: City of Fort Worth (Tarrant County, Fort Worth ISD)

neighborhoods.name: TCU & Berkeley
neighborhoods.home_age: Mostly 1920s to 1950s homes in Berkeley Place and around TCU, with townhome and multifamily infill near campus.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard to large city lots with mature trees; smaller infill lots near University Drive and Berry Street.
neighborhoods.hoa: Most single-family streets have no HOA; newer townhomes and condos usually do.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Tarrant County Hospital District (JPS), Tarrant County College and Tarrant Regional Water District levy property taxes alongside Fort Worth ISD. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown Fort Worth is about 10 minutes north via University Drive or I-30. Dallas means an I-30 drive of 45 minutes or more, and north Dallas job centers are far.
neighborhoods.development: TCU and Endeavor are building Morado on Berry, a 780-bed student housing project with 25,000 square feet of retail on West Berry Street, expected before the 2027-28 school year.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The TCU area mixes the campus and its game-day energy with Berkeley Place's 1920s-50s homes on tree-lined streets. Forest Park, the zoo and Trinity Trails are close by.
cons: More rental housing close to campus

rows.label: City of Fort Worth (Tarrant County, Fort Worth ISD)

neighborhoods.name: West 7th & Cultural District / Arlington Heights
neighborhoods.home_age: Arlington Heights homes are mostly 1920s to 1940s; West 7th townhomes and apartments are mostly 2010s to present.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: Standard older lots in Arlington Heights; small, dense sites around West 7th.
neighborhoods.hoa: Arlington Heights single-family streets generally have no HOA; West 7th townhomes and condos usually do.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Tarrant County Hospital District (JPS), Tarrant County College and Tarrant Regional Water District levy property taxes alongside Fort Worth ISD. Properties along Camp Bowie Boulevard may fall in the Historic Camp Bowie PID. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: Downtown Fort Worth is a few minutes east on West 7th Street or I-30. Dallas is a 45-minute-plus I-30 drive.
amenities: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
Amon Carter Museum of American Art
neighborhoods.development: The $1.7 billion Westside Village broke ground in March 2026 on the former Fort Worth ISD headquarters site at University Drive. Its first phase includes an office building and 308 homes. The eight-story Van Zandt project is underway at West 7th and Foch.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: The Cultural District holds Fort Worth's major museums, Dickies Arena and the Will Rogers complex. West 7th adds dense dining and apartments, and Arlington Heights offers older homes on brick-paved Camp Bowie.
cons: Older Arlington Heights homes need updates

rows.label: City of Fort Worth (Tarrant County, Fort Worth ISD)

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Fort Worth & Sundance Square
neighborhoods.home_age: Historic early-1900s buildings converted to lofts, plus condos and apartments from the 1990s to present.
neighborhoods.lot_profile: No private lots to speak of; housing is condos, lofts and apartments.
neighborhoods.hoa: Condo HOAs are standard, with dues tied to building amenities and age.
neighborhoods.tax_profile: City of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Tarrant County Hospital District (JPS), Tarrant County College and Tarrant Regional Water District levy property taxes alongside Fort Worth ISD. Downtown PID 1 adds an assessment, and Panther Island has its own PID. Check the exact address.
neighborhoods.commute_profile: TRE runs to Downtown Dallas and TEXRail runs to DFW Airport, and Trinity Metro's free downtown Blue Line circulates locally. Driving to Dallas is 45 minutes or more on I-30.
neighborhoods.development: Texas A&M-Fort Worth opened its Law and Education Building in August 2026 and broke ground on an 11-story research building due in 2029. The convention center is in a phased expansion.
neighborhoods.lifestyle_summary: Downtown Fort Worth centers on Sundance Square's 35 blocks of plaza, dining and entertainment, plus Bass Hall. The Texas A&M campus and convention center work are adding activity.
pros: Lower pricing than central Dallas towers
cons: Long drive to Dallas job centers
